> **The intervention demonstrably works &mdash; recovery-rate uplift is 9.909176 pp with a Newcombe&nbsp;1998 95% confidence interval of [4.910346, 14.672446] pp that excludes zero &mdash; but it is not demonstrated to pay: net incremental expected value is Rs&nbsp;60,416.30 with a stratified-bootstrap 95% interval of [-17710.12, 136362.60] that crosses zero, so this project establishes that the system works, not that it pays.**

**Works ≠ pays.** These are two different claims:

- *The intervention works* — contacting a failed-payment customer causes more
  recoveries than not contacting them. The count-basis uplift and its
  confidence interval **exclude zero**, so this is established on the corpus.
- *The intervention pays* — the rupee value of those extra recoveries exceeds
  what it costs to chase them, at a confidence level you would bet on. The
  value-weighted interval **crosses zero**, so this is **not** established.

This project establishes the first claim and is honest that it has not
established the second. A recovery system that is measured only on raw recovery
rate (or only on a point estimate of rupee value) would report a win here; the
discipline of this project is refusing to.

## Why the value case is weaker than the count case

The count basis asks *how many* extra payments recovered. The value basis asks
*how much money* those recoveries were worth — and per-customer recovered value
is zero-inflated and heavy-tailed (most customers recover nothing; a few recover
a large ticket). A mean of that distribution has wide sampling error at
n = 485 control, so the bootstrap interval on incremental value is wide enough
to straddle zero even though the point estimate is solidly positive. More
control customers would narrow it; see *What would change the verdict* below.

The full count-vs-value decomposition (arm balance, small-ticket skew of the
incremental band, the residual the skew does not explain) is in the README's
generated block and in `results/final_run.json`'s `value_vs_count_note`.

## Known limitations — do not read the numbers without these

1. **The corpus outcomes are simulated.** Whether a customer recovers is
   resolved by [`eval/environment.py`](eval/environment.py) from the latent
   per-customer parameters in `data/ground_truth.json` (written by our own
   `datagen.py`), *not* observed from a payment processor. The only real
   recovery signal the system can consume is a live `payment.captured` webhook —
   and there are **none** in this data. Every uplift and EV figure is therefore
   a property of the generator; what the run validates is the *measurement
   apparatus*, not real-world performance.

2. **Phone coverage in the synthetic corpus is 0%.** The action ladder has five
   rungs (`retry_silent`, `email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `agent_call`); the last
   three require a phone number. With no phone numbers, the ladder collapses to
   **email-only** for every decision. `sms`, `whatsapp` and `agent_call` are
   implemented and unit-tested but **never ran against data** — their
   effectiveness numbers in `config/decision_policy.json` are placeholders.

3. **`ROUTE_TO_HUMAN` and `BLOCKED/*` never fired on this corpus.** Zero routed
   decisions, zero guardrail blocks. Those paths are covered by **tests only**
   (`tests/test_slice12_trace.py`, `tests/test_slice12_screens.py`, and the
   7-shape fixture `tests/fixtures/trace_demo.db`). The dashboard's
   [`/queue`](#screens) and the `BLOCKED/*` group on
   [`/not-chased`](#screens) render honest empty states on real data.

4. **The LLM classifier is shipped barred from money actions and is
   unvalidated.** `app/llm_diagnosis.py` runs only on the one ambiguous
   error-code cell; `TAIL_ACT_ENABLED` is `False`, so any LLM-sourced diagnosis
   is recorded and routed to the human queue, never allowed to spend. It is
   barred because the synthetic corpus's `error_description` is a 1:1
   transcription of `error_reason`, so the model would score a fake 1.00. It
   stays barred until validated against real description variation.

5. **There is no time-windowed attribution in the live system.** A recovery is
   a static per-customer counterfactual draw with no time component
   (`attribution_window` is `"none"` on every corpus row). The **72-hour
   window** is applied *at analysis time* only — the `/metrics` LIVE panel
   counts a `payment.captured` as a recovery only when it lands within 72h of
   the failure. Nothing in the pipeline enforces or records that window.

## The numbers

The evidence table is in the generated block above. In prose:

- Count-basis uplift is **9.909176 pp** (Newcombe 95% CI **[4.910346,
  14.672446] pp**), roughly 112 extra recoveries across 1,126 treated
  customers.
- Net incremental EV is **Rs 60,416.30** with a stratified-bootstrap 95% CI of
  **[−17710.12, 136362.60]** — the point estimate is a five-figure gain, the
  interval says we cannot rule out a loss.
- On the demo database (`data/demo.db`, served read-only at `/not-chased`) the
  system withheld contact from **485 control-arm customers holding
  Rs 416,630.00 in ticket value** — deliberately, so their unaided recovery
  rate is the baseline the uplift is measured against.

## What would change the verdict

- **A real recovery feed.** Run the same pipeline (`app.pipeline.process_failure`
  is unchanged) against live webhooks with observed `payment.captured` events.
- **A larger control arm.** `results/final_run.json`'s own
  `synthetic_provenance_note` estimates that pushing the net-EV lower bound above
  zero at the observed effect size needs the sampling error to shrink ~1.3×,
  i.e. a control arm on the order of **~810 customers** (about 2× the current
  485) — a few thousand customers total at the locked 70:30 split.
- **Phone coverage**, to exercise and calibrate the `sms` / `whatsapp` /
  `agent_call` rungs.
- **A validated LLM tail**, before `TAIL_ACT_ENABLED` is ever flipped.

## Reproducing

```bash
python scripts/run_corpus.py final --out results/final_run.json   # byte-identical
python scripts/render_readme_numbers.py --check                   # docs match source
python -m pytest -q                                               # full suite
```

`run_corpus.py final` is deterministic: `now_utc` for every event comes from that
event's own committed `created_at`, arms and outcomes are pure hashes of
`(seed, customer_id)`, floats are rounded to 6 dp, keys sorted. Re-running
produces a byte-identical artifact.
